title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
interviewTips: Clarify: array is sorted non-decreasing, must modify in-place and return k; what should be beyond k? (don't care).
Trade-off: extra array is simpler but O(n) space violates in-place requirement; two pointers achieves O(1) extra space by exploiting sorted order.
Edge-case tip: handle empty array, single element, all duplicates, and all unique; never use nums[k] before checking k bounds.

approaches.name: Approach 1: Brute Force with Extra Array
approaches.intuition: Since array is sorted, duplicates are adjacent. Collect first occurrence of each distinct value into a separate list, then copy it back to the front of original array. Simple to reason about but uses extra space.
approaches.theory: Scan from left to right. Keep nums[0]. For i>0, nums[i] is new unique iff nums[i] != nums[i-1] due to sorted order. Append all such values to temp list expected. Then overwrite nums[0..m-1] with expected and return m = len(expected). This preserves order and uniqueness.

timeComplexity.explanation: One pass to build expected list plus one pass to copy back, each O(n) where n = nums.length.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Extra array holds up to n unique elements in worst case of all distinct.

approaches.name: Approach 2: Two Pointers In-Place Overwrite
approaches.intuition: Use slow pointer k for next write position (length of unique prefix) and fast pointer i to scan. Because sorted, nums[i] is new unique iff it differs from last written element nums[k-1]; then write it at nums[k] and advance k.
approaches.theory: Maintain invariant: nums[0..k-1] are sorted unique and are the uniques of nums[0..i-1]. Initially k=1, i=1. For each i, if nums[i] != nums[k-1], then nums[i] is larger than all in prefix (sorted), so extend prefix by nums[k]=nums[i], k++. Else duplicate, skip. By induction invariant holds at end, k is answer. In-place overwrite is safe because k <= i always.

timeComplexity.explanation: Single linear scan with fast pointer i from 1 to n-1, each element visited once with O(1) work.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Only two integer pointers k and i, modifies array in-place with no extra allocation.

edgeCases: Already unique [1,2,3,4] -> every element copied to itself, k=n
